original_question: Let W be a finite Weyl group with L = ||, let C be a conjugacy class in W, and let C_min be the subset of elements of C having minimal length. For w in C, define N^w in A = Z[v, v^{-1}] to be the trace of the A-linear map H -> H given by h -> v^{2|w|} T_w h T_{w^{-1}}, where H is the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of W. For w in C_min, the paper states that N^w depends only on C, and it calls C positive when N^w belongs to N[v^2]. Determine all positive conjugacy classes when W is a Weyl group of type B_n or D_n.
target_in_paper: Open problem 236*: "Make a list of all positive conjugacy classes in W, assuming that W is a Weyl group of type B_n or D_n."
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target and most of the needed setup: it restricts to the equal-parameter finite Weyl-group case L = ||; it introduces C_min as the minimal-length part of a conjugacy class; it defines the trace polynomial N_w using the same normalization as the open-problem paper; it notes that N_w is constant on C_min; it uses the paper’s positivity criterion N_w in N[v^2]; and it asks for the classification specifically for Weyl groups of types B_n and D_n.
missing_details: The official problem is a classification problem across all ranks n for which the types B_n and D_n are defined, not just for one fixed n.

To make the question fully stand-alone, the Iwahori-Hecke algebra H should be defined explicitly: H is the free A-module with basis {T_w ; w in W} and relations (T_s + v^{-1})(T_s - v) = 0 for simple reflections s and T_x T_y = T_xy when |xy| = |x| + |y|.
The length |w| should be identified explicitly as the Coxeter length function on W.
It should be stated that positivity is attached to the common value of N_w for w in C_min, so the choice of w in C_min is irrelevant.

To stay faithful to arXiv:2006.08535, one should make clear that the identity class is not excluded a priori; the same paragraph notes that for type A_n the positive classes are {1} and the Coxeter class.

The paper’s official formulation is simply to make a complete list of positive conjugacy classes in type B_n or D_n; it does not ask for unequal parameters, arbitrary finite Coxeter groups, or any geometric reformulation.
refined_question: For every rank n for which the type is defined, let W be the finite Weyl group of type B_n or D_n, equipped with its Coxeter length |.|, and let H be the equal-parameter Iwahori-Hecke algebra over A = Z[v, v^{-1}] with basis {T_w}_{w in W} and relations (T_s + v^{-1})(T_s - v) = 0 for simple reflections s and T_x T_y = T_xy whenever |xy| = |x| + |y|. For a conjugacy class C in W, let C_min be the set of elements of C of minimal length, and for w in W define N_w in A to be the trace of the A-linear endomorphism h |-> v^{2|w|} T_w h T_{w^{-1}} of H. Since N_w lies in Z[v^2] and is constant on C_min, call C positive when this common polynomial belongs to N[v^2] (in the sense of arXiv:2006.08535, so the identity class is allowed if it satisfies the definition). Classify all positive conjugacy classes in the Weyl groups of types B_n and D_n.
justification: The draft is aiming at the fourth open problem in the paper, namely 236*, and not at a broader neighboring question. The surrounding paragraph in section 3 of arXiv:2006.08535 supplies exactly the notions your draft expands: finite W with L = ||, the trace polynomial N_w, its constancy on C_min, and the definition of a positive conjugacy class. The refined version keeps that exact scope while adding only the implicit details needed to make the problem fully self-contained: the Hecke algebra relations, the Coxeter-length convention, the quantifier over all ranks n, and the convention that positivity here follows the 2006.08535 setup, which does not exclude the identity class. The earlier paper arXiv:1805.03772 is useful only for confirming the same notation and nearby context, plus the facts that regular elliptic classes are positive and that partial low-rank lists were computed, but the actual research target here remains the unsolved classification problem 236*.
